headline.text: On 28 February 2026, war involving Iran led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. Still showing in the data: about 3 ships a day in the latest reading to 22 November 2026, compared with about 83 ships a day usually at this time of year.

In October 2026, the World Bank's fertilizer price index stood at 148 (2010 = 100), 6% higher than a year earlier. Prices: DAP US$803 a tonne; Urea US$420 a tonne. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is about 8% below the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. Across all the series in this group, one is outside the range of past years.

Grain elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years. It is about 2% above the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. A new high or low on a figure that climbs year after year is the normal state, not a warning: it is the pace that would make it one. The Canadian Grain Commission normally publishes weekly, but has published nothing since 4 October 2026, 55 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.

Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. It is about 4% above the typical level. It is falling much faster than usual for this time of year. It has not yet passed the range of past years, so this is the earlier of the two signals. The Canadian Grain Commission normally publishes weekly, but has published nothing since 4 October 2026, 55 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.

We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data. Four of the 12 are also rising or falling unusually fast, but no product sets off both checks at once. Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada normally publishes every business day, but has published nothing since 19 November 2026, 9 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.
In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

Of the 7 chains of knock-on effects we follow, 2 show signs of a shock moving along them. The furthest is “fertilizer imports are cut before seeding”, where the evidence has reached the link we call “stored supply is used up”.

The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, run by the United Nations and the European Commission, lists eight serious disasters around the world. Three are in countries Canada buys food or farm supplies from. That tells us where to look; it does not mean Canada is affected.

happening.title: Ships through key sea lanes
happening.text: Ships through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 3 a day over the four weeks to 22 November 2026. In the same weeks of the past five years the typical figure was about 83 a day. That is below the range of every one of those years, about 96% below the typical level. Also unusual: Bab el-Mandeb Strait (fewer ships than usual).

happening.title: Weather warnings
happening.text: Five weather alerts were in effect in three provinces or territories when we last checked, including three warnings.

happening.title: Drought on the Prairies
happening.text: At the end of October 2026, 37% of southern Alberta, 0% of southern Saskatchewan and 25% of southern Manitoba were in moderate drought or worse. In Alberta, the province with the most drought, it is inside the range of the past three years for this time of year. It is about 52% below the typical level.

happening.title: Drought where imported produce grows
happening.text: In the week of 24 November 2026, 4% of California; 9% of Arizona; 4% of Florida; 59% of Washington was in moderate drought or worse. Unusual for the time of year: Arizona (less drought than in any of the past five years). Across all the series in this group, one is outside the range of past years.

happening.title: Food recalls
happening.text: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency issued 21 food recall notices in the 30 days to 25 November 2026. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. It is about 16% below the typical level.

happening.title: Strikes and lockouts
happening.text: There were 74 strikes and lockouts under way in Canada in September 2026, three of them in transportation. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. It is about 34% above the typical level.

happening.title: Disasters abroad
happening.text: Eight serious disasters listed worldwide in recent weeks; three in countries that supply Canada.

happening.title: Government announcements
happening.text: 4 announcements about food or farming from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency or Public Safety Canada in the last 30 days.

reach.title: Tropical Cyclone MURASU-26
reach.text: India supplied 27% of the rice Canada imported in 2025, and one other product we track. India is a large country, so the disaster may be far from where these are grown.

reach.title: Tropical Cyclone CHAMPI-26
reach.text: China supplied 7% of the crustaceans (incl. shrimp) Canada imported in 2025. China is a large country, so the disaster may be far from where these are grown.

reach.title: World food and energy prices
reach.text: In October 2026, the World Bank's food price index stood at 122 (2010 = 100), 15% higher than a year earlier. Energy prices were 89% higher than a year earlier. It has not yet passed the range of past years, so this is the earlier of the two signals. Across all the series in this group, two of the five set off both checks.

reach.title: Diesel prices
reach.text: Diesel at self-serve pumps averaged 262.9 cents a litre across five cities in October 2026, 71% more than a year earlier. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years, after allowing for inflation. It is about 51% above the typical level. It is rising much faster than usual for this time of year. Both checks agree, so this one is worth a closer look.

reach.title: The Canadian dollar
reach.text: One US dollar cost $1.42 Canadian on average so far in November 2026, 1.0% more than a year earlier. A weaker Canadian dollar makes imported food and farm inputs dearer. absorbs.text: Railways carried 4.2 million tonnes of wheat, other grains and canola in September 2026. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. absorbs.title: Cargo loaded at Canadian ports
absorbs.text: Ships loaded an estimated 1.6 million tonnes a week at the Port of Vancouver in the four weeks to 20 November 2026. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. It is about 11% above the typical level. Elsewhere, unusual: Prince Rupert (less than usual). Across all the series in this group, one is outside the range of past years.

absorbs.title: What farmers pay for inputs
absorbs.text: In the quarter starting April 2026, the prices Canadian farmers paid for all inputs stood at 187 on Statistics Canada's index (2020 = 100), 11% higher than a year earlier. Fertilizer alone was 24% higher. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years. It is about 20% above the typical level. It is rising a little faster than usual for this time of year, but not enough to stand out. A new high or low on a figure that climbs year after year is the normal state, not a warning: it is the pace that would make it one. Across all the series in this group, three of the four are moving unusually fast and one is outside the range of past years.

feels.title: Grocery prices compared with wages
feels.text: In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

feels.title: Store prices for everyday foods
feels.text: We follow 15 everyday foods in Canadian stores. In September 2026, two cost more and three cost less than in the same month of any of the past five years, after allowing for inflation. Higher than usual: ground beef, whole chicken. Across all the series in this group, one of the 15 set off both checks.

feels.title: Grocery price rises by province
feels.text: In October 2026, grocery prices were up most in Quebec (+3.0% on a year earlier) and least in Prince Edward Island (+0.1%). The national figure was +2.0%.

feels.title: People who struggle to afford food
feels.text: In 2024, 24.0% of people in the ten provinces lived in a household that struggled to afford food, up from 16.8% in 2018. Among children it was 30.8%. This survey is published once a year, more than a year after the fact.

questions.text: There is more grain in storage than in any recent year at this time. Is that a comfortable reserve, or grain waiting for trains and ships?

Wholesale prices for strawberries from the United States and peppers from Ontario are higher than in any recent year at this time. Is the cause weather where they are grown, the exchange rate, or something else?
Fewer ships than usual are passing through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Which Canadian imports and exports use these routes, and what are the alternatives?
Diesel costs more than at this time in any recent year, after inflation. How much of that reaches farm costs and grocery prices, and how soon?
